# onetsolutions_hosting_addon_domain (Resource)

Manages an addon domain of a web hosting: another domain served by the same account, from its own directory.

The web hosting must be active, and the plan of the web hosting must allow another addon domain.
An addon domain cannot be changed in place: changing any argument removes it, with the files of
its directory left in place, and adds the new one. Terraform refuses to add a domain the web
hosting already serves; import it instead. The site is reachable once the domain's DNS points at
the web hosting.

If the addon domain is removed or its directory changed outside Terraform, the next plan adds it
again or replaces it. Once the web hosting is cancelled or terminated, the next refresh removes the
addon domain from the state.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "onetsolutions_web_hosting" "site" {
  domain = "example.com"
}

resource "onetsolutions_hosting_addon_domain" "shop" {
  hosting_id    = data.onetsolutions_web_hosting.site.id
  domain        = "example-shop.fr"
  document_root = "public_html/example-shop.fr"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `domain` (String) The domain to serve, such as `example.org`: lowercase, without a trailing dot. Its DNS must point at the web hosting for the site to be reachable. Changing it recreates the addon domain.
- `hosting_id` (String) The UUID of the web hosting the addon domain belongs to. Changing it recreates the addon domain.

### Optional

- `document_root` (String) The directory the domain serves, relative to the account's home directory, such as `public_html/example.org`. When unset, the web hosting's default directory for the domain; the state then holds the absolute path the web hosting reports. Changing it recreates the addon domain.
- `organization_id` (String) The organization the object belongs to. Defaults to the provider's `organization_id` when the object is created; changing it explicitly recreates the object.
- `project_id` (String) The project the object belongs to. Defaults to the provider's `project_id` when the object is created; changing it explicitly recreates the object.
- `subdomain` (String) The internal subdomain of the main domain the addon domain is attached to: letters, digits and hyphens, without dots, 63 characters at most. When unset, derived from the domain (`example-org` for `example.org`). Changing it recreates the addon domain.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The addon domain, same as `domain`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = onetsolutions_hosting_addon_domain.shop
  id = "3f2a9c1e-5b7d-4e8f-9a0b-1c2d3e4f5a6b/8b1d4e2f-6c3a-4f9e-8d7b-2a1c0e9f8d7c/9a0b1c2d-3e4f-4a5b-8c6d-7e8f9a0b1c2d/example-shop.fr"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# <organization_id>/<project_id>/<hosting_id>/<domain>, or <hosting_id>/<domain> when the provider sets organization_id and project_id.
terraform import onetsolutions_hosting_addon_domain.shop 3f2a9c1e-5b7d-4e8f-9a0b-1c2d3e4f5a6b/8b1d4e2f-6c3a-4f9e-8d7b-2a1c0e9f8d7c/9a0b1c2d-3e4f-4a5b-8c6d-7e8f9a0b1c2d/example-shop.fr
```
